# C++20 profile

The C++20 language and library features Kokeb Labs code may use, the rules each one comes with, and the ones it may not
use, as numbered guidelines. They extend MISRA C++:2023, which is written for C++17, to the C++20 our code is written
in, and they define exactly what deviation MD-CPP-001 covers. The C++20 profile page explains each feature's verdict;
categories follow MISRA's model (mandatory and required guidelines are `must`, advisory ones `should`).

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Verified |

## KB-CPP20-001: Strict ISO C++20, with a conformance build on every target compiler { #kb-cpp20-001 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Every target a repository builds itself (library, tests, fuzzers, host examples, install consumer) compiles as ISO C++20
with `CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF` and `-pedantic-errors`. Every public header also compiles on its own at `-std=c++20
-pedantic-errors` with each compiler the repository ships for: host GCC and Clang, Arm GCC in the cross-build, and the
ESP-IDF toolchain, whose own default dialect is newer (a header self-check compiled at `-std=c++20` inside the ESP-IDF
build).

*Why:* MD-CPP-001 deviates Rule 4.1.1 for C++20, not for whatever a framework enables. CMake's default leaves extensions
on (`-std=gnu++20`), and ESP-IDF builds as `gnu++23` or `gnu++26`, so without a strict build a GNU extension or a C++23
feature compiles on one toolchain and breaks on another.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/cmake-extensions` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `forbidden-patterns/cmake-cxx-standard` (implemented): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter
  names the pattern set
- `compiler-warnings/-pedantic-errors` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror
- `strict-dialect` (implemented): every public header, and through the driver header its src/\*.ipp, compiles as ISO
  C++20 (-std=c++20 -pedantic-errors, extensions off) with each compiler the repository ships for: host GCC and Clang,
  Arm GCC in the cross-build, and the ESP-IDF toolchain through a header self-check built at -std=c++20 inside the
  ESP-IDF build, whose own default dialect is newer

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-a)

## KB-CPP20-002: Only profile features; nothing from C++23 or later { #kb-cpp20-002 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Target code uses only the language and library features this profile marks \*Use\* or \*Use with rules\*, under the
guidelines attached to them, and library headers only from the layer's ADR-0017 subset. No feature of C++23 or later is
used, even where a framework's dialect accepts it (`std::to_underlying`, `std::byteswap`, `std::expected`, `if
consteval`, `[[assume]]`, deducing `this`, the `uz` literal suffix).

*Why:* MD-CPP-001 must name what it covers, and a feature that enters without review enters the safety case unexamined.
Our own `detail::ToUnderlying` replaces the C++23 helper at no cost.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/forbidden-features` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `strict-dialect` (implemented): every public header, and through the driver header its src/\*.ipp, compiles as ISO
  C++20 (-std=c++20 -pedantic-errors, extensions off) with each compiler the repository ships for: host GCC and Clang,
  Arm GCC in the cross-build, and the ESP-IDF toolchain through a header self-check built at -std=c++20 inside the
  ESP-IDF build, whose own default dialect is newer
- `include-allowlist/driver` (implemented): a script over the include graph that fails on a header outside the allowed
  set for the directory; the parameter names the table (driver, hosted, kb-core, handlers, hal-boundary)
- `include-allowlist/target` (implemented): a script over the include graph that fails on a header outside the allowed
  set for the directory; the parameter names the table (driver, hosted, kb-core, handlers, hal-boundary)
- review: A C++20 feature not in the profile joins it and MD-CPP-001 in one pull request, or is not used.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-a)

## KB-CPP20-003: Nothing C++20 deprecates { #kb-cpp20-003 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

No construct deprecated by C++20: compound assignment or `++`/`--` on a `volatile` object, `volatile` parameters and
return types, implicit capture of `this` through `[=]`, a comma expression in a subscript, arithmetic or comparison
between two different enumeration types or between an enumeration and a floating-point type.

*Why:* Deprecated features are candidates for removal and are deprecated because they mislead: a `volatile`
read-modify-write is not atomic, and `[=]` does not copy the object.

*Verified by:*

- `compiler-warnings/-Wdeprecated` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror
- `compiler-warnings/-Wdeprecated-enum-enum-conversion` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and
  -Werror
- `compiler-warnings/-Wdeprecated-enum-float-conversion` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag
  and -Werror
- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-misleading-capture-default-by-value` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from
  config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 10.1.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-a)

## KB-CPP20-004: No feature-test macros to choose behaviour { #kb-cpp20-004 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

Shared code does not test `__cpp_` or `__cpp_lib_` macros or include `<version>` to pick an implementation. There is one
language level; a missing feature is a toolchain problem, not a branch.

*Why:* Two code paths per feature means one of them is untested on any given CI matrix.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/forbidden-features` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 19.0.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-a)

## KB-CPP20-005: Every template parameter is constrained by a named concept { #kb-cpp20-005 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Each type template parameter in target code has a constraint: a named concept in the template head (`template <SpiPort
Port>`) or a `requires` clause. A callable parameter is constrained with `std::invocable` and its result type.

*Why:* An unconstrained parameter accepts anything; misuse is reported deep inside the body, or compiles.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/unconstrained-template` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Every new template parameter names its concept.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 17.8.1; MISRA C++:2023 Dir 0.3.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-b)

## KB-CPP20-006: Port concepts check the exact hook signature and `noexcept` { #kb-cpp20-006 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A port concept accepts only hooks with exactly the signature on the driver's Porting page: each argument is probed with
a type that converts to the documented parameter type and to nothing else, each compound requirement states `noexcept`,
and each result type is checked with `std::same_as`. Compile-fail tests prove that a narrowed parameter and a missing
`noexcept` are rejected.

*Why:* A concept that probes with plain values is satisfied by `Transfer(..., uint16_t len)`, so the driver's length is
truncated at every call without a diagnostic; KB-CPP-035 asks for `noexcept`, and the concept is where it can be proved.

*Verified by:*

- `compile-fail-tests` (implemented): a misuse of the public API is a compile error, proved by a test that must fail to
  compile
- `codeql/port-hook-signature` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Each port concept probes with `detail::Exactly<T>` and states `noexcept` on every hook.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.6; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.1.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.3

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-b)

## KB-CPP20-007: Optional hooks use named detection concepts; a misdeclared hook is an error { #kb-cpp20-007 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Each optional hook has a named concept `Has<Hook>` in `<chip>::detail` that checks argument types exactly, the result
type and `noexcept`, and a `Declares<Hook>` concept that only tests the name; the driver `static_assert`s
`!Declares<Hook> || Has<Hook>`. No anonymous requires-expression appears in an `if constexpr` condition.

*Why:* Detection that silently falls back when a hook is misdeclared turns a wiring mistake into a missing delay or a
dropped GPIO error; one named concept is also what KB-CPP-036 asks for.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/inline-requires` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `compile-fail-tests` (implemented): a misuse of the public API is a compile error, proved by a test that must fail to
  compile

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.1.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 9.6.5

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-b)

## KB-CPP20-008: One dependent-false helper { #kb-cpp20-008 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

A branch that must never be instantiated fails with `static_assert(detail::kAlwaysFalse<T>, "...")`, from one `template
<typename> inline constexpr bool kAlwaysFalse = false;` per repository, not with ad hoc spellings such as `sizeof(T) ==
0`.

*Why:* C++20 does not allow `static_assert(false)` in a discarded template branch; one named helper states the intent.

*Verified by:*

- review: Discarded branches use `detail::kAlwaysFalse`.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.0.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-b)

## KB-CPP20-009: Code that does not depend on the port lives outside the class template { #kb-cpp20-009 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

Register encoders and decoders, validation, CRC, unit conversion and error text are namespace-scope `constexpr`
functions, not members of the driver's class template.

*Why:* A member of `Driver<Port>` is emitted once per port type; a free `constexpr` function is emitted once or folded
away, and can be proved with `static_assert`.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/port-independent-member` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: A static member that never names the port moves out.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.2.3

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-b)

## KB-CPP20-010: Abbreviated function templates are constrained and stay out of the public API { #kb-cpp20-010 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

A function parameter declared `auto` has a type-constraint (`std::unsigned_integral auto`), and public driver member
functions have no `auto` parameters.

*Why:* `void f(auto x)` is a template that instantiates for every argument type, `bool` and `char` included, and hides
that from the reader and the code-size budget.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/unconstrained-auto-parameter` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No `auto` parameter in public driver API.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 17.8.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-b)

## KB-CPP20-011: Concepts carry meaning; overloads are not chosen by subsumption { #kb-cpp20-011 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

A concept names a contract a reader can state in one sentence. Driver code does not build overload sets chosen by
concept subsumption, and does not define concepts that every type satisfies; a choice between behaviours is an `if
constexpr` on a named concept.

*Why:* Subsumption depends on the exact spelling of atomic constraints, so a harmless edit can switch the chosen
overload without a diagnostic.

*Verified by:*

- review: No two overloads differ only in one being more constrained.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 17.8.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-b)

## KB-CPP20-012: Pure computations are `constexpr` and proved with `static_assert` { #kb-cpp20-012 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A function that computes only from its arguments (register encoder or decoder, frame builder, CRC, unit conversion,
`Validate`) is `constexpr`. Each such function in a `_registers` or `_types` header is named in at least one
`static_assert` with a datasheet value; an encode and decode pair has a round-trip `static_assert`; each preset asserts
`Validate(preset) == Error::Ok`; and an array whose size mirrors a register count uses the named constant.

*Why:* A `static_assert` is evidence that costs nothing at run time and runs on every compiler, and undefined behaviour
inside a constant evaluation is a compile error, so the vectors are also proved free of it.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/unasserted-constexpr` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Every new pure function has a datasheet `static_assert`; encode and decode pairs a round trip.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.0.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.3

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-013: `consteval` only for build-time construction { #kb-cpp20-013 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0

`consteval` is used for what must never run at run time: checked configuration values, generated tables, validated
constants. A failed check calls a declared but undefined function whose name states the error. A `consteval` check never
replaces the run-time validation of a value that can come from outside the build.

*Why:* A board's configuration is usually a constant, and rejecting a bad one at build time is better than at boot; the
run-time `Validate()` stays for everything else.

*Verified by:*

- review: The run-time `Validate()` call stays in the start-up path.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.1.2; MISRA C++:2023 Dir 0.3.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-014: `constinit` on every mutable static { #kb-cpp20-014 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Every object with static storage duration that is not `constexpr` (the cases MD-CPP-005 allows) is declared `constinit`.
Drivers have no such objects (KB-CPP-040).

*Why:* `constinit` turns constant initialisation from a review claim into a compiler error and closes the static
initialisation order hazard.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-avoid-non-const-global-variables` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from
  config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database
- `codeql/constinit` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter names the
  query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop, pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Every mutable static is `constinit`.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.7.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.7.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-015: `if constexpr` only on compile-time facts, each branch instantiated by a test { #kb-cpp20-015 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

The condition of `if constexpr` depends on a template parameter or a build-configuration constant, and each branch of a
hook dispatch is instantiated by at least one host test (a minimal port and a full port).

*Why:* A discarded branch is not compiled for that instantiation, so a branch no test instantiates is unverified code.

*Verified by:*

- `coverage-floor/level` (implemented): gcovr coverage of library code by the host tests at or above the floor
  (coverage-floor/level for lines and branches, coverage-floor/mcdc for condition coverage), as ADR-0020 defines it
- review: The tests have a minimal and a full port, so both branches compile.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.0.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.0.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-016: No `std::is_constant_evaluated` { #kb-cpp20-016 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

Code does not branch on `std::is_constant_evaluated()`.

*Why:* Inside `if constexpr` it is always true, a classic mistake; outside it, two implementations of one function have
to be kept equivalent, and the clean form is C++23.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/forbidden-features` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.0.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-017: Header-scope variables are `constexpr` { #kb-cpp20-017 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A variable defined in a header at namespace scope is `inline constexpr`; a static data member of a class template is
`static constexpr`. No mutable `inline` variable exists.

*Why:* An `inline` variable is one object for the whole program, so a mutable one is a global by another name.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-avoid-non-const-global-variables` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from
  config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database
- `codeql/mutable-inline-variable` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.2.4; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.2.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.7.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-018: Configuration-dependent inline code: one configuration per program { #kb-cpp20-018 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A header whose inline function bodies depend on configuration macros (`<chip>_kconfig.hpp`, or anything that uses
`__has_include` for configuration) is a leaf: no other library header includes it, every translation unit of one program
sees the same configuration, and its file comment says so.

*Why:* Different macro values in two translation units give two definitions of one inline function: an ODR violation
with no diagnostic.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/kconfig-leaf` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter names
  it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features, feature-test
  macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- review: The Kconfig header's comment states one configuration per program.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.2.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-019: No allocation and no virtual functions in constant evaluation { #kb-cpp20-019 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

`constexpr` code does not use `new`, `std::allocator` or an allocating container, and no function is `constexpr
virtual`.

*Why:* C++20 allows transient allocation during constant evaluation, but the headers that offer it are outside the
target subset, and the same code would run with the heap at run time.

*Verified by:*

- `forbidden-patterns/heap` (implemented): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the
  pattern set
- `include-allowlist/driver` (implemented): a script over the include graph that fails on a header outside the allowed
  set for the directory; the parameter names the table (driver, hosted, kb-core, handlers, hal-boundary)

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 21.6.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 21.6.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-c)

## KB-CPP20-020: Every shift count is provably below the operand width { #kb-cpp20-020 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category mandatory; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A shift whose count is not a constant is preceded, in the same function, by a check or a mask that bounds the count
below the width of the promoted left operand. A public helper that shifts by an enumeration or an integer argument masks
the count itself.

*Why:* A shift by the width or more is undefined behaviour, and an `enum class` with a `uint8_t` base can hold any value
from 0 to 255, so being an enumeration proves nothing.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/clang-analyzer-core.BitwiseShift` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the
  CMake compile database
- `sanitizers` (implemented): host tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
- `codeql/shift-range` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter names the
  query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop, pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Every run-time shift count is masked or checked in the same function.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.4; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.3

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-021: Bit work in `uint32_t`; no promoted narrow operands; no platform-width types { #kb-cpp20-021 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Operands of `~`, `<<`, `>>`, `&`, `|`, `^` and arithmetic on register values are `uint32_t` (or `uint64_t`) before the
operator; `uint8_t` and `uint16_t` values are cast up first. `unsigned`, `unsigned long`, `int` and the `UL` suffix
never set a width: literals are `uint32_t{1}`, or `1U` when the other operand is already `uint32_t`. A loop counter used
as a shift count is unsigned.

*Why:* Narrow unsigned values promote to signed `int`, and `unsigned long` is 32 bits on our targets but 64 bits on the
host, so host tests cannot show a width bug.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/hicpp-signed-bitwise` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake
  compile database
- `codeql/narrow-bitwise-operand` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Narrow operands are widened to `uint32_t` before bit operations; no `UL` widths.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.5; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.4; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.9.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-022: Narrowing is explicit, compound assignment included { #kb-cpp20-022 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Every conversion to a narrower or differently signed integer type is a `static_cast` where it happens, including the
hidden one in `|=`, `&=`, `+=`, in initialisation, argument passing and return. A value whose range is not proved by a
mask or a preceding check is tested with `std::in_range<T>` first.

*Why:* `-Wconversion` is silent when it can prove the value fits, so the conversion stays unseen until the commercial
checker runs; an explicit cast is also where a reviewer looks for the range argument.

*Verified by:*

- `compiler-warnings/-Wconversion` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror
- `clang-tidy/bugprone-narrowing-conversions` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the
  CMake compile database
- `codeql/compound-narrowing` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No `uint8_t |= unsigned` style compound assignment.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.6

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-023: Mixed-sign comparison through `std::cmp_less` and its siblings { #kb-cpp20-023 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0

When a signed and an unsigned value must be compared, the code uses `std::cmp_less` (or `cmp_equal`, `cmp_greater`, ...)
instead of a cast.

*Why:* A cast picks a direction and can wrap; the C++20 functions compare the mathematical values.

*Verified by:*

- `compiler-warnings/-Wsign-compare` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.5

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-024: Signed reinterpretation of wire values through a named helper { #kb-cpp20-024 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A same-width signed value read from a wire or register comes from `std::bit_cast<intN_t>` or `static_cast<intN_t>` (both
defined in C++20) inside a named helper whose comment states the encoding; an N-bit field narrower than its container is
sign-extended by a named helper in `int32_t` arithmetic. Never through a union, `memcpy` or a pointer cast.

*Why:* C++20 fixed two's complement and made the conversion modular, but the encoding should be named once.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-union-access` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run
  with the CMake compile database
- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-reinterpret-cast` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy,
  run with the CMake compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 12.3.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.8.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.2.5

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-025: Integer-to-enum conversion only for proven enumerators { #kb-cpp20-025 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category mandatory; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

`static_cast<E>(x)` from a non-constant integer is allowed only when every value `x` can take is an enumerator: the
mask's range equals the contiguous enumerator set, stated by a `static_assert` next to the enumeration, or the value is
checked first and a non-enumerator becomes an `Error`.

*Why:* A non-enumerator in an enumeration defeats every `switch` and every `==` test that follows.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/enum-from-integer` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Each integer-to-enum cast is preceded by a range check or proof.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.3; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 10.2.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-026: One enumeration utility layer { #kb-cpp20-026 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

Conversion to the underlying type goes through one `detail::ToUnderlying` function template, and range checks through
one `detail::IsEnumerator` with an `EnumLast<E>` class template specialised next to each contiguous enumeration.
Function templates are never explicitly specialised.

*Why:* Hand-written `static_cast<uint8_t>(x) > static_cast<uint8_t>(Last)` checks must each be updated when an
enumerator is added.

*Verified by:*

- review: Enumeration range checks use `detail::IsEnumerator`.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 17.8.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-027: `using enum` only at block scope { #kb-cpp20-027 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

`using enum E;` appears only inside a function body, never at namespace or class scope in a header.

*Why:* At namespace scope it exports every enumerator into the enclosing namespace and undoes the scoping that scoped
enumerations exist for.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/using-enum-scope` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: `using enum` only inside function bodies.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.4.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 10.2.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-028: `<bit>` for counting and rotation instead of hand-written loops { #kb-cpp20-028 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0

Population count, leading and trailing zero counts, single-bit tests and rotations use `std::popcount`,
`std::countl_zero`, `std::countr_zero`, `std::has_single_bit`, `std::bit_width`, `std::rotl` and `std::rotr`. On a
timing-critical path the generated code is checked once per target.

*Why:* They accept only unsigned types, are `constexpr` and are simpler to review than a loop.

*Verified by:*

- review: Bit counting uses `<bit>`.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.4; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 9.5.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-029: `std::bit_cast` between equal-size values, never for byte order { #kb-cpp20-029 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

`std::bit_cast` is used only between trivially copyable value types of the same size, never to or from a pointer, and
never to read a multi-byte wire value: byte order is always explicit shifts. `std::endian` appears only in a
`static_assert` or in MCU port code.

*Why:* A `bit_cast` of a 4-byte buffer to `uint32_t` silently assumes the host byte order (KB-CPP-106).

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/bugprone-bitwise-pointer-cast` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the
  CMake compile database
- `codeql/bit-cast-byte-order` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No `bit_cast` from a byte array.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.2.5; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.2.4; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.2.6; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.8.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-030: Strong types for units and easily swapped parameters { #kb-cpp20-030 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

A public function with two or more adjacent parameters of the same arithmetic type but different meanings, or a physical
quantity whose unit is easy to confuse, takes single-member strong types (`Milliamps`, `Microseconds`, `I2cAddress7`):
trivially copyable aggregates of one integer with only the operations the unit supports.

*Why:* `CurrentCode(uint32_t ma, uint32_t rref_ohm)` compiles with the arguments swapped; a one-member struct is passed
in a register on the Arm and Xtensa ABIs, so the safety costs nothing.

*Verified by:*

- review: Adjacent same-typed parameters with different units use strong types.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.6

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-d)

## KB-CPP20-031: Designated initialisers for configuration; every member has a default { #kb-cpp20-031 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Every member of a configuration or value aggregate has a default member initialiser. Code that sets more than one member
of such an aggregate in one expression uses designated initialisers; positional brace initialisation of a multi-member
aggregate is used only inside the type's own header.

*Why:* C++20 already orders designators and forbids mixing; the defaults make an omitted designator mean the datasheet
default, and designators keep a call site right when a field is inserted.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/modernize-use-designated-initializers` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with
  the CMake compile database
- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-member-init` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run
  with the CMake compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 11.6.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 15.1.4; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.6

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-e)

## KB-CPP20-032: No parenthesised aggregate initialisation { #kb-cpp20-032 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Aggregates are never initialised with parentheses (`Config(a, b)`).

*Why:* The C++20 parenthesised form is positional and, unlike braces, allows narrowing, so `Config(1000, 2.5)` compiles;
it also reads like a constructor that does not exist.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/paren-aggregate-init` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Aggregates use braces.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.0.6

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-e)

## KB-CPP20-033: Defaulted `operator==` only on exactly comparable members { #kb-cpp20-033 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

`operator==` of a value type is defaulted, never hand-written, and only when every member is an integer, `bool`,
enumeration, `std::array` of those, or a type that itself follows this guideline. Types with floating-point or pointer
members have no `operator==`.

*Why:* A defaulted `==` compares floats exactly and pointers by address, which is rarely what the same configuration
means.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/float-defaulted-equality` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No defaulted `==` on a type with a float or pointer member.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 16.6.1; MISRA C++:2023 Dir 0.3.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-e)

## KB-CPP20-034: No three-way comparison in drivers { #kb-cpp20-034 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Drivers do not declare or use `operator<=>` and do not include `<compare>`. Libraries may default `<=>` for a type with
a genuine total order, under KB-CPP20-033's member rules.

*Why:* Driver configurations, statuses and errors have no order, and `<compare>` is outside the driver subset.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/forbidden-features` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `include-allowlist/driver` (implemented): a script over the include graph that fails on a header outside the allowed
  set for the directory; the parameter names the table (driver, hosted, kb-core, handlers, hal-boundary)

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 16.6.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-e)

## KB-CPP20-035: Structured bindings test the error before the value { #kb-cpp20-035 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0

Structured bindings may decompose an aggregate returned by value. When it is a `Result`, the error binding is tested
before the value binding is read. Bindings are by value, or `const auto&` to a named object.

*Why:* `[[nodiscard]]` is satisfied by the binding, so the compiler no longer helps when the value is used first.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/structured-binding-order` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: The error binding is tested first.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.1.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 11.6.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-e)

## KB-CPP20-036: Class-type template arguments are structural and integral { #kb-cpp20-036 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library · since 1.0

A class type used as a non-type template parameter has only public integral, `bool` and enumeration members: no
floating-point members, no pointers.

*Why:* Integral members keep instantiation identity obvious and portable across our compilers.

*Verified by:*

- review: Class NTTPs have integral members only.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 17.8.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-e)

## KB-CPP20-037: `[[nodiscard]]` on every error-carrying type { #kb-cpp20-037 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

`Result<T>`, `Result<void>`, every `Error` enumeration and every status type are declared `[[nodiscard]]` on the type,
and every `const` query member function is `[[nodiscard]]`. A deliberate discard is a `(void)` cast with a comment
saying why.

*Why:* With the attribute on the type, every function returning it is covered, `Validate()` and bus helpers included,
and the compiler proves what review used to.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/nodiscard-error` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `compiler-warnings/-Wunused-result` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror
- `clang-tidy/bugprone-unused-return-value` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the
  CMake compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.1.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-f)

## KB-CPP20-038: `[[maybe_unused]]` instead of `(void)` for conditionally used names { #kb-cpp20-038 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0

A parameter or variable used only in some `if constexpr` branches is declared `[[maybe_unused]]`; a `(void)x;` statement
is kept for discarding a result.

*Why:* It keeps `(void)` meaning one thing: an explicit discard.

*Verified by:*

- `compiler-warnings/-Wunused-parameter` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.2.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-f)

## KB-CPP20-039: No `[[fallthrough]]` { #kb-cpp20-039 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Every non-empty `switch` clause ends with `break`, `return` or a `[[noreturn]]` call; `[[fallthrough]]` is not used.

*Why:* The attribute documents a fall-through our switch layout does not allow at all; adjacent case labels already
cover several values with one action.

  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `compiler-warnings/-Wimplicit-fallthrough` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror

## KB-CPP20-041: No `[[no_unique_address]]` in drivers { #kb-cpp20-041 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Drivers do not use `[[no_unique_address]]`, and no type whose layout is asserted (KB-CPP-009) uses it anywhere.

*Why:* It lets members overlap, which changes size and offsets differently per compiler, so layout assertions pass on
one and fail on another.

*Verified by:*

  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)

## KB-CPP20-042: Caller buffers are spans, with a fixed extent when the size is known { #kb-cpp20-042 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A function in target code that takes a buffer takes `std::span<T>` or `std::span<const T>`, with a fixed extent when the
size is a property of the chip or the frame, and a dynamic extent only when the caller chooses the count.
Pointer-and-length pairs exist only in the port hook signatures (KB-CPP-035), where the driver passes `.data()` and
`.size()` of an array or span it owns.

*Why:* The size travels with the pointer, so the callee can check it, and a fixed extent turns the check into a compile
error. MD-CPP-001's justification relies on it.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/pointer-length-parameter` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the
  parameter names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No pointer-and-length parameter outside port hooks.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.11.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.7.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-g)

## KB-CPP20-043: A dynamic span is checked before it is indexed, wherever it is indexed { #kb-cpp20-043 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Before the first element access, a function that receives a dynamic-extent span checks its size against the contract
(not empty, not above the documented maximum, the output at least as large as the input). A helper that copies into a
fixed buffer checks the length itself instead of trusting its callers. `first`, `last` and `subspan` take only counts
proved in range. Host tests and fuzzers build with the standard library's assertions, so an out-of-range access traps.

*Why:* C++20 `std::span` has no checked `at()`; an out-of-range `operator[]`, `first(n)` or `subspan` is undefined.

*Verified by:*

- `library-hardening` (implemented): host tests and fuzz targets build with the standard library's assertions
  (\_GLIBCXX\_ASSERTIONS, libc++ hardening), so an out-of-range span or array access traps
- `sanitizers` (implemented): host tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
- `codeql/unchecked-span-index` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Every dynamic span is size-checked before its first access.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.7.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.3

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-g)

## KB-CPP20-044: Views and references never outlive what they refer to { #kb-cpp20-044 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category mandatory; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A `std::span` (and above the drivers a `std::string_view`) is never a data member, never returned when it refers to a
local or a temporary, and never built from a temporary container. A lambda that captures by reference is never stored or
returned. A member function that returns a reference into `*this` is `&`-qualified, with the rvalue overload deleted.

*Why:* Dangling access is undefined behaviour that tests reusing the stack the same way never show, and since C++17 a
non-copyable driver can be a temporary.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/bugprone-dangling-handle` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake
  compile database
- `codeql/span-member` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter names the
  query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop, pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No span member; reference accessors are `&`-qualified.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.8.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.8.3; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.8.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.8.4

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-g)

## KB-CPP20-045: Lambdas: explicit captures, local use, no state { #kb-cpp20-045 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Lambdas in target code list every capture (`[this, address]`, never `[=]` or `[&]`), are not `mutable`, are called
within the full expression or passed down the stack to a constrained template, and are never stored beyond the enclosing
function. No lambda calls itself.

*Why:* A default capture hides what a closure depends on, a stored closure is a lifetime hazard, and recursion breaks
the stack bound.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-misleading-capture-default-by-value` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from
  config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database
- `codeql/lambda-capture` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter names
  the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop, pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Every lambda capture is explicit.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.1.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.1.2; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 7.11.3

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-h)

## KB-CPP20-046: No lambdas in unevaluated operands or at namespace scope in headers { #kb-cpp20-046 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

No lambda appears in `decltype`, `sizeof`, a template argument or a default template argument, and no header defines a
namespace-scope variable initialised with a lambda.

*Why:* Every lambda expression has its own type, so the same declaration in two translation units names different types:
an ODR trap with no diagnostic.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/lambda-unevaluated` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter
  names the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop,
  pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No lambda in an unevaluated operand.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 6.2.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-h)

## KB-CPP20-047: No generic lambdas in drivers { #kb-cpp20-047 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template · since 1.0

Drivers do not use `[]<typename T>(...)` or `auto` lambda parameters; a generic helper is a named, constrained function
template in `detail`.

*Why:* A generic lambda is an unconstrained template (KB-CPP20-005) that is harder to read in review.

*Verified by:*

- `codeql/generic-lambda` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter names
  the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop, pointer-length-parameter)
- review: No generic lambda in driver code.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 17.8.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-h)

## KB-CPP20-048: `std::optional` is read only when engaged, never through `.value()` { #kb-cpp20-048 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category mandatory; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

`*opt` and `opt->` are used only where a test of `opt.has_value()` (or `if (opt)`) dominates them; `.value()` is never
called. Failure is modelled with `Result`, not `std::optional`: an optional means may be absent, and that is fine.

*Why:* Dereferencing an empty optional is undefined behaviour, and `.value()` throws, which with `-fno-exceptions` ends
the program.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/bugprone-unchecked-optional-access` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with
  the CMake compile database
- `clang-tidy/bugprone-optional-value-conversion` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with
  the CMake compile database
- review: No `.value()` on an optional.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.3; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.1.2; MISRA C++:2023 Dir 0.3.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-i)

## KB-CPP20-049: No `variant`, `any`, `function` or `expected` in drivers { #kb-cpp20-049 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Drivers do not use `std::variant`, `std::any`, `std::function` or `std::expected`. Libraries may use `std::variant` with
`std::get_if` or `std::visit` over an exhaustive overload set, never `std::get`.

*Why:* `std::get` and `std::visit` on a valueless variant throw, `std::function` may allocate, `std::any` needs RTTI,
and `std::expected` is C++23.

*Verified by:*

  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `include-allowlist/driver` (implemented): a script over the include graph that fails on a header outside the allowed
  set for the directory; the parameter names the table (driver, hosted, kb-core, handlers, hal-boundary)

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 21.6.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-i)

## KB-CPP20-050: Range algorithms with rules; no views in target code { #kb-cpp20-050 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Non-allocating algorithms from `<algorithm>`, the `std::ranges::` overloads included, may be used on named arrays and
spans with side-effect-free predicates. `<ranges>` and range views are not used in target code.

*Why:* The algorithms are bounded loops with clear contracts; views evaluate lazily and hold references, so a lifetime
error moves away from where it is written, and they are slow in unoptimised debug images.

  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `include-allowlist/driver` (implemented): a script over the include graph that fails on a header outside the allowed

## KB-CPP20-054: `<numbers>` for mathematical constants { #kb-cpp20-054 }

**SHOULD** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0

Mathematical constants come from `<numbers>` (`std::numbers::pi_v<float>`) wherever the layer's ADR-0017 subset includes
it, never as hand-typed digits.

*Why:* Constants only, no code; it removes hand-typed digits and the suppression that goes with them.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/modernize-use-std-numbers` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake
  compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Dir 0.3.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-i)

## KB-CPP20-055: `std::atomic_ref` only for lock-free sharing with an interrupt { #kb-cpp20-055 }

**SHOULD** · hal, firmware · since 1.0

HAL code may use `std::atomic_ref<T>` for an object shared with an interrupt handler only when
`std::atomic_ref<T>::is_always_lock_free` is asserted and every access to the object goes through it.

*Why:* It makes a plain member atomic without changing its type, but mixing atomic and plain access is a data race.

*Verified by:*

- review: A `static_assert` of `is_always_lock_free` sits next to each `atomic_ref`.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 10.1.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-i)

## KB-CPP20-056: No coroutines { #kb-cpp20-056 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

No `co_await`, `co_yield` or `co_return`, and no `<coroutine>`.

*Why:* The coroutine frame is heap-allocated unless the optimiser removes it, which is not guaranteed; the generated
state machine is hard to bound for stack and timing; and the RTOS task model already gives concurrency.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/forbidden-features` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)
- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-avoid-capturing-lambda-coroutines` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from
  config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 21.6.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.2.10

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-j)

## KB-CPP20-057: No modules { #kb-cpp20-057 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

No `import`, `export module`, module partitions or header units.

*Why:* ESP-IDF's build does not support them, GCC's support is partial, CMake needs a scanning generator, and the
analysis tools lag; header-only drivers gain little.

*Verified by:*

- `cpp20-profile/forbidden-features` (implemented): a source check of the C++20 profile (rules/cpp20.yml); the parameter
  names it: forbidden-features (no coroutines, modules, range views, &lt;format&gt;, char8\_t, C++23 features,
  feature-test macros, [[fallthrough]], and in drivers no &lt;=&gt;, &lt;source\_location&gt;, variant, any, function or
  [[no\_unique\_address]]), cmake-extensions (every CMakeLists.txt that builds a target sets CMAKE\_CXX\_EXTENSIONS OFF,
  itself or in a parent directory), nodiscard-error (Error enumerations and Result types are [[nodiscard]]),
  inline-requires (no requires-expression in an if constexpr condition), kconfig-leaf (no header includes the Kconfig
  header)

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.1

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-j)

## KB-CPP20-058: Loops are bounded by a validated constant { #kb-cpp20-058 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Category required; warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, template, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A loop whose bound comes from configuration or input compares its counter with `<` against a bound that `Validate()` or
a preceding check limited to a named maximum. `<=` against an unsigned bound that can be the type's maximum is not used,
a `for` condition has one counter comparison and no extra error flag, and one index never serves two different arrays.

*Why:* `ms <= timeout` with `timeout == UINT32_MAX` never ends because the counter wraps; a bounded loop is what lets us
state the worst-case time of a call.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/bugprone-too-small-loop-variable` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the
  CMake compile database
- `codeql/unbounded-loop` (planned): a query of the Kokeb CodeQL pack for C++ over the CMake build; the parameter names
  the query (for example shift-range, compound-narrowing, enum-from-integer, unbounded-loop, pointer-length-parameter)
- review: Every loop bound from configuration or input is validated against a named maximum.

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 9.5.1; MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.0.2

*Explained in:* [standards/cpp20-profile.md](../standards/cpp20-profile.md#part-j)
